opennyai_summary.2_September_2025__facts: The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No.98 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Bindki, District-Fatehpur with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
opennyai_summary.2_September_2025__arguments:
Only one witness has been examined during trial, as such, there is no likelihood of early conclusion of trial.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is in jail since 17.04.2024, as such, applicant has been in incarceration for about more than one year and four months and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the bail application and placed reliance on the certified copy of the statement of P.W.2 who has been examined on 27.08.2025 and has nominated the applicant.
It is further argued that FIR is prompt and the deceased expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant, as such, applicant is not entitled for bail.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
8. The Supreme Court in case of X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr., 2024 INSC 909, has held that once the trial has commenced, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion, which may either result in conviction or acquittal of the accused.
The bail should not be normally granted to the accused after the charge has been framed.
It should also not be granted by looking into the discrepancies here or there in the deposition.
11. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgments of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
opennyai_summary.2_September_2025__decision:
10. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.
12. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
4. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
The applicant is husband of the deceased and their marriage has taken place on 16.06.2022.
Learned counsel further submitted that the informant has stated in his statement before the trial court that his daughter (deceased) has committed suicide.
Learned counsel has referred the statement of the concerned doctor and submitted that it is a case of suicide and not the case of strangulation.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 24.02.2023.
The cause of death of the deceased has been shown ante-mortem strangulation.
Referring the statement of concerned Doctor, it was submitted that she was done to death by way of strangulation.
7. Perusal of record shows that deceased has suffered death due to strangulation within short period of six months of her marriage with the applicant.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
8. Considering submissions of learned counsel for the parties and all attending facts, no case for bail is made out.
9. Accordingly, the second bail application of the applicant Arjun is hereby rejected.
10. However, the trial court is directed to expedite the proceedings of trial and to conclude the same as early as possible preferably within a period of ten months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
